common_name: La Marne Rose (Earth-Kind Pink-and-White Bicolor Polyantha)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil; La Marne, introduced in 1915, is a Texas A&M Earth-Kind designated rose recognized for exceptional disease resistance and low-input performance.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. La Marne, a French polyantha introduced in 1915, bears large clusters of single to semi-double flowers combining bright pink outer petals with a paler pink-to-white center, a cheerful bicolor pattern produced almost continuously from spring through frost on a dense, well-branched, arching shrub. It has earned Texas A&M's Earth-Kind designation, a rigorous field-trial recognition given only to roses that thrive with minimal water, fertilizer, and pesticide input, reflecting its outstanding disease resistance and tolerance of heat, humidity, and less-than-ideal soil. Its graceful, fountain-like habit and reliable bloom make it a strong low-maintenance choice for a mixed border, informal hedge, or mass planting. Prune lightly in late winter to shape; otherwise it thrives on neglect.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Earth-Kind Rose Trials
